content.title: Render From State, Don’t Manually Control the UI
content.hook: You already learned how to change a page directly with browser JavaScript.
content.context:
React encourages a different loop:

```text
change the data
→ describe the UI for that data
→ React updates the screen
```

You do not need to manually find a paragraph and tell it to display a different string every time state changes.
goals: Replace imperative “make this element do X” thinking with declarative rendering from current state.

content.title: Compare the mental models
content.text:
**Imperative:**

> Find the status element. Change its text. Hide this button. Show that message.

**Declarative:**

> When `saved` is true, render the saved message. When it is false, render the unsaved message.

The second description matches the state of the application.

activities.title: Change the state, not the display command

content.question:
Imagine `saved` is state.

What should the click handler primarily do?

options.text: Find the paragraph and manually replace its text.
Set `saved` to the new value and let rendering decide what to display.

feedback.correct: The state is the source of truth for the rendered result.
feedback.incorrect: The state is the source of truth for the rendered result.

feedback.correct: `saved` already determines what the paragraph renders. Direct DOM editing creates a second source of truth.
feedback.incorrect: `saved` already determines what the paragraph renders. Direct DOM editing creates a second source of truth.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** In React, the UI is a consequence of current state and props.
**Senior habit:** If a component is manually editing the same UI that React renders, pause and ask whether there are now two sources of truth.
nextSteps: Refactor one imperative UI update into state-driven rendering and explain why the second source of truth is dangerous.
